title: IANN: A Unified Framework for Equivariant InterAtomic Neural Networks with User-Friendly Implementation
abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN functionals. Additionally, IANN provides an agent interface to facilitate integration with autonomous agents.

title: Mixed-Sign Kitaev Exchange in Jahn-Teller-Distorted CrI$_2$
abstract: Kitaev couplings with ferromagnetic (FM) or antiferromagnetic (AFM) character shape magnetic frustration and phases differently in real materials, yet their coexistence within a single material remains unexplored. Here, we propose Jahn-Teller distortion as a route to realizing such coexistence on inequivalent bonds. First-principles calculations identify monolayer CrI$_2$ as such a system, with AFM and FM Kitaev couplings on the short and long bonds, respectively. These opposite signs are robust against variations in Hubbard $U$, functionals, and strain. A minimal tight-binding model links this sign contrast to Jahn-Teller-split $t_{2g}$ orbitals and their hopping to $e_g$ orbitals. We further adopt the cluster expansion method and develop a realistic machine-learned spin Hamiltonian, which reproduces the experimentally observed proper-screw geometry and propagation direction and reveals highly nonuniform spin rotation, with turning angles ranging from $48.0^\circ$ to $93.9^\circ$. Both proper-screw anisotropy and strong anharmonic spin rotation arise from the mixed-sign Kitaev interaction. These findings not only establish Jahn-Teller distortion as a microscopic route to mixed-sign Kitaev exchange, but also open a new avenue for exploring novel magnetic phases.

title: Hidden Heat-Current Transport Channels Behind Observable Temperature Dynamics
abstract: Diffusive decay and wave-like oscillations in temperature dynamics are commonly used to characterize heat conduction, yet these signatures do not uniquely identify the underlying heat-current transport mechanisms. Here we reveal a spectrum of constitutive heat-current channels whose microscopic organization can change without a corresponding qualitative change in observable temperature dynamics. We develop a two-level spectral theory that first resolves the finite-wave-vector constitutive response into relaxational and streaming channels characterized by their poles and heat-current residues, and then connects their combined response to equilibrium temperature fluctuations through energy conservation. First-principles calculations for NaF at 17~K reveal that the same streaming-induced mode coupling responsible for the perturbative nonlocal correction in the Guyer--Krumhansl (G--K) reduction drives a nonperturbative transformation of the isolated momentum-organized relaxational channel into a dominant complex-conjugate streaming pair. This transformation breaks down the single-relaxational-channel constitutive structure of G--K, while oscillatory temperature dynamics persist below the short-period boundary of its predicted oscillatory window. At shorter periods, heat-current weight redistributes among multiple collision-coupled streaming channels before approaching independently damped phonon streaming. Increasing temperature provides a distinct route beyond hydrodynamics by eliminating the isolated momentum-organized sector, even as oscillatory temperature dynamics persist. Thus, the breakdown of a hydrodynamic constitutive description can reflect a reorganization of heat-current transport rather than the disappearance of oscillatory temperature dynamics, and agreement with temperature measurements alone does not validate the constitutive structure of a reduced theory.

title: Ferroelectric control of the $K$--$Γ$ valley landscape in R-stacked bilayer WSe$_2$
abstract: In bilayer WSe2 the valence-band maxima at K and Γ lie within a few thermal energies of one another, and gating redistributes holes between a light and a heavy valley of different mobilities on a landscape that stays fixed. We show that rhombohedral (R) stacking moves the landscape itself. The three-fold symmetry of R stacking forbids interlayer tunneling at K but not at Γ. The K coupling is therefore exactly zero, not merely small. A fit that leaves the coupling free returns an upper bound of 0.017 meV, three orders of magnitude under k_BT at room temperature, while the Γ coupling is 361.8 meV. The polarization creates a potential step between the layers and splits the K doublet. Each K state stays on a single layer, so the K edge shifts by half of that splitting, 41.7 meV, which any tunneling would reduce. Γ barely responds. Two consequences follow from symmetry alone, whatever the size of that shift. The two registries, carrying opposite out-of-plane ferroelectric polarizations, are exact mirror images along the displacement-field axis, and reversing the polarization reverses the displacement of the landscape. Their differential-mode transconductances are equal and opposite at zero field, where the response vanishes for an ideal nonpolar reference. The stored polarization is read out as a reversal of sign and not as a difference of current. Sweeping the field is a second route to the same parity. In the ideal symmetric limit the transconductance passes through zero at the field that cancels the polarization, 1.07 V/nm, at a single temperature. Both routes are limited by the symmetry of the device more than by the band structure. Stacking also renormalizes the landscape, so the polar one is not a translated copy of the nonpolar reference. Absolute offsets follow the exchange-correlation functional. The symmetry relations do not.

title: Cross-species digital xenocortication model delineates molecular correlates of human brain connectome
abstract: Cross-species digital xenocortication (CSDX) model based on pairing of a human brain structure with one or more mouse brain structures was constructed and implemented to dissect the molecular correlates of the human brain connectome. Design of the CSDX model is based on the assumption that a human brain region and its named mouse counterpart occupy corresponding positions in an evolutionary conserved mammalian brain connectome plan, so that a projection strength measured between two mouse structures is informative about the relation between the two human structures paired with them. In the CSDX model, gene expression for the node was measured in the human brain, while connection strength between two nodes was measured in the mouse brain. CSDX models of different parcellations were employed to explore the potential regulatory associations of brain connectome patterns and constituents of protein-protein interaction (PPI) cascades of hybrid assembly pathways of endogenous multiprotein complexes. Metrics of continuous engagement of the PPI cascade nucleated protein dimers of CORUM multiprotein complexes have been identified as statistical components of the multivariate transcriptome-connectome associations. It accounts for additional connectome associated variations beyond the five measured axes in the 82 nodes CSDX model. Comparisons of the seven arm models of transcriptome-connectome associations demonstrate that the mouse derived model generally fits the mouse brain connectome better, while the human derived model assigns a significantly larger fraction of its transcriptome-connectome association to unique rather than net shared contributions. This study nominates elite panels of top scoring candidate protein dimers and CORUM multiprotein complexes for follow up mechanistic studies of their potential roles in structural functional features governing mammalian brain connectome.

title: Wearable sensing technologies and machine learning for fatigue assessment in sport horses
abstract: BackgroundFatigue in sport horses is a multifactorial phenomenon that critically affects performance, injury risk, and welfare, yet its real-time, field-based assessment remains an unmet challenge.ObjectivesTo synthesise evidence on the use of wearable sensors and machine learning for fatigue-related monitoring in sport horses and to identify priorities for future fatigue assessment.Study designScoping review.MethodsThis scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Publications from 2015 to 2026 were identified through Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect.

title: Energetics of Coherent Heterophase Interfaces: Separating Chemical and Strain Contributions
abstract: Coherent interfacial energies govern the formation and evolution of multiphase microstructures, but their calculation is complicated by the elastic energy required to accommodate lattice mismatch. Here, we construct a high-throughput DFT database of 365 coherent FCC/FCC, BCC/BCC, and HCP/HCP interfaces involving 41 metallic elements and lattice mismatches of up to 25%. We use the supercell approach, consisting of constructing superlattices of different thicknesses to separate the coherency strain energy from the chemical contribution to the interfacial energy. We classify the results according to the long-range ordering tendency of each binary system and the sign of the calculated interfacial energy. Most phase-separating systems exhibit positive interfacial energies, whereas most compound-ordering systems exhibit negative values, reflecting favorable unlike-atom bonding. Exceptions show that the chemical preference at a particular interface need not coincide with bulk phase behavior: coherency strain can oppose ordering, and stable compounds can adopt structures distinct from the calculated superlattices. No clear correlation of interfacial energy with lattice mismatch is observed, whereas coherency strain energy increases with mismatch. For phase-separating systems, the lowest interfacial energies generally occur along the closest-packed orientations, while this trend is absent for ordering systems. Comparisons with reported interfacial energies and binary phase diagrams show qualitative consistency, although quantitative agreement varies with reference states, structural constraints, and temperature. The database provides a systematic reference for metallic coherent heterophase interfaces and demonstrates the importance of separating strain and chemical energy contributions when interpreting alloy behavior.

title: Non-proteinogenic γ-aminobutyric acid reorganises L-arginine and L-lysine adsorption on Ca-montmorillonite through selective displacement and Ca 2+ bridging
abstract: Prebiotic polymerisation in dilute aqueous solution is frustrated by hydrolysis, and mineral surfaces are a widely invoked route by which this bottleneck may have been overcome on early Earth and Mars. Smectite clays are strong candidates, because their permanent layer charge allows their hydrated basal surfaces to concentrate, orient and protect organic molecules. Natural organic inventories are mixtures rich in non-proteinogenic amino acids, yet adsorption on clays has been studied almost entirely one compound at a time.

title: Biomolecular design through latent reasoning with RFD4-Proteina
abstract: Biomolecular design requires finding chemically and geometrically compatible arrangements of interacting atoms and molecules. The complexity of problems which can be tackled by deep learning design models is limited by both the molecular landscape they encompass and their ability to explore that landscape effectively. Here we introduce RFD4-Proteina, which addresses these limitations through intrinsic and extrinsic reasoning within a shared chemical and conformational latent space.

title: Colloidally Prepared Homogeneous Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Efficient Tandem Solar Cells with Industrial Silicon
abstract: Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites, based on mixed halide-cation compositions, are widely employed as top cells in perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells to overcome the theoretical limitations of single-junction devices and exploit the full potential of crystalline silicon photovoltaics. However, uncontrolled nucleation rates and disordered crystallization kinetics in WBG perovskites pose a grave challenge to the preparation of phase-homogeneous perovskite films.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Rare Constitutional Centromeric Expansion of Chromosome 1 in a Phenotypically Normal Individual: A Comprehensive Cytogenetic Study
abstract: Constitutional centromeric heteromorphisms are uncommon chromosomal variants that may complicate cytogenetic interpretation. We report a constitutional enlargement of the centromeric region of one chromosome 1 homologue identified incidentally during biological dose estimation in a suspected occupationally exposed individual. Conventional cytogenetics, pancentromeric fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and multiplex FISH confirmed the variant and excluded cryptic chromosomal rearrangements. Analysis of 500 metaphases revealed no dicentric chromosomes. Quantitative assessment demonstrated a centromere to chromosome length ratio of 0.314 plus/minus 0.019 for the enlarged homologue compared with 0.169 plus/minus 0.019 for the unaffected homologue and 0.161 to 0.186 in controls, representing an approximately 1.86 fold increase (t = 28.4, p < 0.0001). The findings establish a benign constitutional centromeric heteromorphism of chromosome 1 and highlight the importance of distinguishing such variants from structural chromosomal abnormalities during routine cytogenetic evaluation.

title: Chemo- and Regioselective Dehydrogenative Allylic C–H Oxygenation of Ketones
abstract: Allylic ethers and alcohols are prevalent structural motifs in natural products and pharmaceuticals as well as versatile building blocks for organic synthesis. Transition-metal-catalyzed oxidative allylic C–H functionalization represents one of the most straightforward tools for the rapid assembly of allylic ethers. However, current methods typically suffer from selectivity issues and limited scope.

title: Interface-Selective Extreme Ultraviolet Second Harmonic Generation Away from Linear Absorption Edges
abstract: Extreme ultraviolet (XUV) second harmonic generation (SHG) combines interface selectivity with core-level element specificity but has so far been limited to linear absorption edges. Here, we measure XUVSHG from an indium tin oxide capped MoO$_3$/SiO$_2$/Si photovoltaic heterojunction for fundamental energies of 60--76\,eV, below the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge. Where linear absorption is a featureless valence background, we observe a strong, structured XUVSHG response with maxima near 70 and 76\,eV. Layer-resolved first-principles calculations reproduce both maxima and assign them to the Si/SiO$_2$ interface, the 76\,eV peak to the bridging Si monolayer and the 70\,eV peak to the near-interface substrate. Bethe--Salpeter calculations for bulk Si connect the signal to Si 2$p$ excitons at 140--160\,eV. At the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge, the calculated response is instead governed by MoO$_3$-induced asymmetry at the oxide interface. These findings establish off-edge XUV SHG as a powerful approach for selectively probing distinct buried interfaces within complex material heterostructures.

title: MT-RGCN-DTI: A Multi-Task Relational Graph Convolutional Network for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction
abstract: Prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) has become a very crucial part of drug discovery. With the increase in the data volume, it has become very important to improve prediction accuracy by integrating multiple data sources. In this regard, utilising multiple resources in the form of heterogeneous information network to address DTI prediction can be rewarding. In this work, we propose a heterogeneous information network based multi-task DTI prediction model which leverages the advantages of relation graph convolutional network (RGCN). To achieve this, the model employs drug-target interaction network, drug-drug similarity network and protein-protein similarity network to construct a heterogeneous information network. Moreover, we use a knowledge graph embedding scoring functions to model interactions between drug and targets, specifically DistMult and ComplEx as decoders over the learned node representations. We performed extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and compared with state-of-the-art methods. We observed that the proposed model shows competitive performance, thereby confirming the effectiveness of our approach. The codes and datasets are available at https://github.com/Dheeran-S/MT-RGCN-DTI/.

title: Two channels of magnetic renormalization in the terahertz lattice response of FePS$_{3}$
abstract: Interlayer vibrations probe how magnetic van der Waals layers are stacked and coupled. In the zigzag antiferromagnet FePS$_3$, ultrafast experiments show that the interlayer shear couples strongly to the magnetic order, but not how magnetism renormalizes the shear stiffness and damping. Here, using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we measure the anisotropic conductivity of FePS$_3$ from 1.6 to 300 K and in fields up to 7 T normal to the layers. We observe absorption bands at 0.6-0.8 and 1.3-2.4 THz that persist into the paramagnetic phase. The lower one is consistent with an interlayer shear resonance; the magnetic order stiffens one of its in-plane components and softens the other, reversing their splitting at the Néel temperature. We identify two channels of magnetic renormalization: frequency shifts are confined to the ordered phase, whereas the linewidths of this resonance and most oscillator strengths follow short-range spin correlations persisting well above the transition. The field acts mainly on the higher resonance in one orientation: near 3.2 T, its softening accelerates and its linewidth has a cusp-like minimum, consistent with critical slowing down of a field-induced order parameter. These results give an equilibrium view of spin-shear coupling, which is anisotropic and persists above the Néel temperature through short-range correlations.

title: Surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides
abstract: Magnetically intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides are layered materials with highly tunable magnetic orders and unconventional transport properties. Here we report a surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in $\mathrm{M}_{1/3}\mathrm{T}\mathrm{X}_{2}$, in which the surface and bulk favor distinct magnetic orders. In $\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) results are reproduced by an A-type antiferromagnetic electronic structure, while neutron scattering and bulk DFT+$U$ calculations identify stripe order as the bulk ground state. DFT+$U$ slab calculations resolve this contradiction by showing that relaxation of an Fe-terminated surface reverses the magnetic preference from stripe to A-type order. The same dichotomy recovers the $K$-centered Fermi-surface pockets that are observed in $\mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Ta}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ but absent from previous bulk calculations. Notably, the surface-stabilized magnetic phase of $\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ carries nonrelativistic spin splitting and can exhibit altermagnetic character. These results caution against the general association of ARPES signals with bulk magnetic states in these systems, and suggest surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy as a promising route to realize magnetic phases, including altermagnetism, that are not energetically favored in the bulk.

title: Matching two-dimensional statistics does not certify three-dimensional transport in battery electrodes
abstract: Three-dimensional battery electrode structures reconstructed from two-dimensional micrographs are routinely used to predict transport, assuming that matching the measured 2D statistics reproduces the relevant 3D properties. We test this premise on X-ray tomograms of three all-solid-state cathodes. With a differentiable conductivity solver, we optimise voxel structures that match the real electrode in phase fractions, boundary density, two- and three-point correlations and lineal-path functions, on all section planes, slab by slab and layer by layer, within measurement noise. Every sample has statistical twins conducting 10-88-fold less than the real electrode, robust to 5^3 majority filtering, whereas the most conductive are at most 3.3-fold above it. The twins rearrange rather than remove material, severing or funnelling through-plane paths. A classifier on 2D sections detects them, as it does current 2D-to-3D generators: the information is in the images but not in the statistics. Matching standard 2D statistics therefore does not certify 3D transport.

title: Robust Antiferromagnetic Ordering above 500 K in a Family of Bilayer van der Waals Materials
abstract: Stabilizing magnetic order above room temperature in layered materials is highly desirable for low-dimensional spintronics applications. However, realizing room-temperature antiferromagnetism in layered magnets remains challenging. Here, we present a layered semiconducting oxyhalide material family, Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$ ($X$ = F, Cl, Br), which exhibits robust high-temperature antiferromagnetic ordering. The two-dimensional nature and scalability of this system are demonstrated by atomically resolving the van der Waals gap of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Br$_2$ and synthesizing centimeter-scale single crystals of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$. Temperature-dependent neutron scattering and magnetization measurements determine their G-type magnetic structure and transition temperature. Remarkably, the Néel temperature of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$F$_2$ ($\sim$580 K) is the highest among all reported layered antiferromagnets. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that strong nearest-neighbor superexchange interactions along both out-of-plane and in-plane directions, particularly the magnetic couplings along lattice $c$ direction within the bilayer motif, are primarily responsible for the high Néel temperatures in Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$. In contrast, inter-bilayer spin couplings are negligibly weak, without much influence on the stabilization of the antiferromagnetic order. Therefore, theoretical calculations predict that this robust antiferromagnetic order could persist or even strengthens at room-temperature even at the monolayer limit. Our results highlight iron-based layered oxyhalides as a promising platform for exploring beyond-room-temperature antiferromagnetism in the two-dimensional limit, holding immense potential in areas like information storage and spin-based devices.

title: Rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculation and master equation analysis of the CNO system in high-energy collisions
abstract: The CNO system governs the formation and depletion of the CN, CO and NO radiative species relevant to combustion, astrophysical and hypersonic applications. The NO($X^2Π$) + C($^3P$), CN($X^2Σ^+$) + O($^3P$) and CO($X^1Σ^+$) + N($^4S$, $^2D$) collisional systems are investigated using rovibrational state-specific quasi-classical trajectory calculations and master equation analysis under hypersonic thermal conditions. Inelastic processes proceed primarily through rotational excitation of low-lying states and rovibrational excitation of high-lying states. For most systems, rotational and vibrational relaxation times exhibit comparable scales and unconventional temperature dependences, invalidating the assumption of decoupled energy modes. Dissociation is governed by high-lying rovibrational states and correlates strongly with the state-specific energy deficit rather than vibrational-specific dynamics. At $T$ = 10,000 K, 72 to 93% of the depletion of the diatomic species occurs within a quasi-steady-state (QSS) regime for all systems. At lower temperatures, a large portion of the depletion occurs outside the QSS regime, indicating that the QSS assumption holds only for moderate to high temperatures. No such regime is established for exchange reactions, demonstrating that the QSS assumption is invalid for modelling them. The NO + C system proceeds predominantly towards CN + O at low temperatures and towards the CO + N channels at high temperatures, preferentially forming N($^4S$). The fraction proceeding towards the CO + N channels remains lower than in available shock-tube measurements, while the thermal exchange rate coefficients reproduce shock-tube measurements and high-fidelity calculations. Finally, consistent similarities across inelastic, exchange and dissociation processes offer promising physical foundations for reduced-order model development.

title: Higher-dimensional homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic materials
abstract: Quasiperiodic geometrical arrangements, which exhibit long-range order in the absence of periodicity, have attracted interest in the design of composites and mechanical metamaterials. In this context, direct numerical simulations explicitly resolving the quasiperiodic microstructure become prohibitively expensive for macroscopic problems, motivating the development of homogenized continuum models. However, the absence of a periodic unit cell in physical space hinders the use of conventional homogenization methods. In the present work, we exploit higher-dimensional periodic representations to perform computational homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic composites. Thereby, effective properties are obtained from unit-cell problems solved using the fast Fourier transform in higher-dimensional spaces. Using two-dimensional Penrose tilings and three-dimensional Ammann--Kramer--Neri tilings as paradigmatic examples, we describe the distribution of heterogeneous material properties in the corresponding higher-dimensional unit cells, compute effective elasticity tensors, and assess convergence of fully resolved finite patches to the homogenized limits. We provide open-source implementations of all numerical models.

title: Analytic Model for Transient Plateau Filling in Vibrational Distributions of Periodically Driven Plasmas
abstract: In periodically driven molecular plasmas, the vibrational distribution function is governed by the competition between vibration--vibration (V-V) up-pumping along the anharmonic ladder and vibration--translation (V-T) relaxation, producing the Treanor--Gordiets distribution. When vibrational energy accumulates across cycles faster than V-V exchange can populate the upper levels, the Gordiets plateau remains transiently depleted. Existing algebraic models assume a quasi-steady plateau, whereas exact transient solutions of the nonlinear V-V diffusion equation require the elapsed time since excitation and the source strength, which are unavailable in multidimensional simulations that track only local macroscopic variables. Here, elapsed time is replaced by a local vibrational energy timescale formed from the vibrational energy per molecule and its period-averaged rate of change. This reduces the diffusion equation in level space to an ordinary differential equation solved in closed form without linearization, yielding a level-dependent correction to the steady plateau governed by a single dimensionless group: the number of V-V collisions per energy timescale weighted by the plateau amplitude at the Treanor minimum. The distribution front advances as the square root of this group, and the steady distribution is recovered as the group grows large. Compared with state-to-state master-equation calculations for N$_2$ under nanosecond pulse trains spanning 300-1500 K, 0.041-1 atm, and 1-100 kHz (1440 sampled states), the model reduces the 90th-percentile error in level populations from 1.88 decades for the steady model and 1.32 decades for an adapted self-similar solution to 0.53 decades, at essentially the evaluation cost of the steady model.

title: Stabilization of LaH$_{10}$ with Thorium: Superconductivity in (La,Th)H$_{10}$ up to 232 K near 1 Mbar
abstract: Ternary lanthanum-based hydrides are among the best high-temperature superconductors. Here we show that substituting La with thorium stabilizes La(Th)H$_{10}$ clathrate structure at $\sim$1 Mbar while only minimally suppressing superconductivity. The resulting cubic (La,Th)H$_{10}$ phase, synthesized from relatively air-stable La$_2$Th, La$_3$Th and La$_5$Th alloys, reaches an onset $\textit{T$_c$}$ = 232 K at 134 GPa, as confirmed by contact resistance measurements. Superconductivity was verified by two independent methods: electrical resistance and contactless radio-frequency measurements under applied magnetic fields at various pressures. Using a record-high pulsed current of 380 mA, we investigated critical phenomena in P6$_3$/mmc-(La,Th)H$_9$ at 173 GPa, which allowed for the experimental determination of a single superconducting gap within the s-wave model: $Δ(0) = 37 \pm 4.5$ meV and $2Δ(0)/kT_c = 4.9 \pm 0.6$. The La-Th-H system is chemically rich: in addition to the decahydride and nonahydride mentioned above, we also identified nanocrystalline I4/mmm-(La,Th)H$_4$ (5-6 nm grain size), (La,Th)H$_6$, as well as $hP13$, $cF80$ and $A15$ phases with compositions of (La,Th)H$_{5.75-6.25}$ and $\textit{T$_c$}$ $\approx$ 83 K at 70-80 GPa, and a possible (La,Th)H$_{16}$ polyhydride.

title: AlphaDiffract: automated crystallographic analysis of powder X-ray diffraction data
abstract: AlphaDiffract: automated crystallographic analysis of powder X-ray diffraction data

title: U-HamGNN: a universal model for magnetic Hamiltonians conditioned on spin and Hubbard U
abstract: The electronic structure of a magnetic crystal depends jointly on its spin configuration and the on-site Hubbard correction U, requiring a separate DFT+U calculation for each combination. We introduce U-HamGNN, an equivariant network that takes these two inputs directly and predicts spin-resolved Hamiltonians across diverse crystal chemistries. A spectral-hybrid optimizer that weights each update direction by how consistently the gradient points along it reaches 8% lower Hamiltonian error than Muon and 26% lower than AdamW in a ten-epoch benchmark. The predicted bands reproduce U-dependent gap opening and altermagnetic spin splitting within the trained window and beyond it; exchange couplings and magnetic-order calls derived from the Hamiltonian agree with DFT+U on a calibration set. This universal model provides a new tool for magnetic research.

title: The microscopic origin of the hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes bundles
abstract: In a recent study we reported large hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in samples made out of Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes (DWCNT) at supercritical temperatures (50 K, 77 K and 150 K), a physical behavior of practical interest. Here, we center our efforts in elucidate its physical origin by means of neutron diffraction (ND) and computer simulations. After a detailed theoretical modeling of the ND signal we were able to quantitatively study how the nanostructure of the material reacts to the hydrogen loads. An expansion of the bundle structure with increasing hydrogen load was found. Taking advantage of the translational symmetry of a DWCNT bundle along the nanotube axis, a two dimensional numerical analogue of the system helped us to clarify the microscopic origin of the hysteresis. Two microscopic mechanisms are identified as responsible for the metastable hydrogen adsorption, one structurally static in character, namely, H$_{2}$-load dependent effective energy barriers between interstitials, the other related to the structural deformation, namely, the opening/closing of the channels between interstitials with increasing/decreasing H$_{2}$ loads owing to the concomitant bundle expansion/contraction.

title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and history frames. Each edited scene thus forms an exact, pixel-level counterfactual pair with its original, which allows us to isolate the causal effect of the inserted object on the predicted trajectory. Evaluating four VLAs and two WAMs, we find that they react weakly, often barely at all. Finally, we test how easily one of the evaluated VLAs, ReCogDrive, can be taught to brake hard for imminent hazards: a short fine-tuning stage on edited scenes substantially improves its reactions, with the learned behavior generalizing to unseen objects and fully real scenes, at minimal cost to nominal driving. These results call into question the out-of-the-box long-tail capabilities of these models, but suggest that they can be a strong foundation for acquiring them with little additional training, highlighting the value of real or synthetic data that demonstrates the long-tail behaviors nominal datasets rarely contain. Code and data will be made publicly available.

title: Self-assembly of dipolar nanoclusters on an attractive substrate: A coarse-grained simulation approach
abstract: Recently, Thomas et al. [Nanoscale 17, 18291 (2025)] showed that bismuth oxido nanoclusters (BiO-NCs) of the type [Bi$_{38}$ O$_{45}$ (Boc-L-Phe-O)$_{24}$] form chains when deposited onto gold or pyrolitic graphite substrates. This chain formation is significantly enhanced when the bismuth in the BiO-NCs is partially replaced by cerium through doping. In this work, we study a simplified, coarse-grained model of this process, namely (magnetic) Stockmayer particles in the presence of an attractive substrate. The model is investigated by means of molecular dynamics simulations. The deposition experiment is mimicked by a rapid quench from high temperature to a low temperature below the bulk coexistence curve. The results are found to be qualitatively similar to the experimental observations reported earlier. In our simulations, we find significant chain formation in the bulk even at rather low concentrations, which is in contrast to the BiO-NCs in ethanol for which dynamic light scattering reveals negligible aggregation in the absence of the substrate. This lends support to a scenario, conjectured in the work of Thomas at al., where the dipole moments are induced by the particle-substrate interaction and hence there is little dipole moment in the bulk. In a second part, we study the system in equilibrium. We consider the scaling of chains, the number of layers populated as a function of two-dimensional density, and we draw analogies to polymers on interfaces, which have been extensively studied over the past decades. Most notably, it is found that the chains behave as self-avoiding walks at low densities, which gives way to rod-like scaling at higher densities.

title: Efficient, Repeatable and Cost-effective 17O-Isotopic Labeling of Proline and Hydroxyproline for 17O-NMR Analyses
abstract: L-Hydroxyproline and L-Proline are two amino acids commonly found in proteins, and which are also used for making cocrystals of pharmaceutical interest. Understanding their local environment and dynamics at the atomic scale using techniques like solid-state NMR is thus of interest. Here, we propose cost-effective and repeatable synthetic strategies to label in oxygen-17 the carboxylic group of these amino acids, and of their Fmoc-derivatives.

title: Cobalt Isolated Single-Atomic Sites for Iso-butane Direct Dehydrogenation with Robust Anti-Coke Deposition
abstract: Developing efficient, coke-resistant catalysts based on earth-abundant metals remains a major challenge for the direct dehydrogenation (DDH) of light paraffins, a reaction commonly catalyzed by costly Pt-based catalysts. Herein, we report a catalyst featuring isolated single-atom Co sites (Co ISASs) that achieve 46% isobutane conversion and 90% selectivity to isobutene at 550 °C. The catalyst maintains stable isobutene selectivity throughout a 24 h stability test, with no coke deposits detected by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy or Raman spectroscopy.

title: Position-Dependent Conformational Landscapes of Flavin–Tryptophan Pairs in Designed Magnetosensitive Protein Maquettes
abstract: Photoinduced electron transfer is a fundamental mechanism in biological energy transduction and signal processing and can generate spin-correlated radical pairs whose subsequent reactivity is modulated by external magnetic fields. Elucidating how the local molecular environment governs the formation and dynamical evolution of such radical pairs remains a major unresolved problem, particularly in biologically relevant settings where multiple electron transfer pathways may operate concurrently.

title: A Multi-Gram Synthesis of 7,12-Dibromo[7]helicene
abstract: Functionalized helicenes offer a concise synthetic entry to chiral optoelectronic materials. Despite the relevance of these building blocks, the structural diversity of known difunctionalized helicenes remains limited, reflecting the synthetic challenges associated with specific substitution patterns. Herein, we report a 10-step synthesis of hitherto unreported 7,12-dibromo[7]helicene in multigram quantities. A single Mallory photocyclization was employed at a late stage, harnessing the bromine substituents as blocking groups to achieve regiocontrol.

title: A Stereocontrolled Synthesis of (4R)-1-Methyl-4-Propyl-L-Proline, the Amino Acid Fragment of Lincomycin
abstract: We present a concise route for the stereoselective conversion of commercial (cis)-4-hydroxy-L-proline into (4R)-1-methyl-4-propyl-L-proline, the amino acid fragment found in the clinically used antibacterial antibiotic lincomycin. Our account of success is accompanied by a discussion of two failed routes. The rise of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the continued search for new antibacterial agents.

title: MIRAL Cloud: Integration and Orchestration for AIEnabled Experimentation
abstract: AI-enabled automated experimentation combines experimental platforms, analysis tools, and robots to support high-throughput screening and adaptive experimental decisions. These capabilities often rely on independently developed software, creating a need to coordinate execution while preserving the scientific context of results. We present MIRAL Cloud, an integration and orchestration system developed for the Material Innovation through Robotics and AI Laboratory (MIRAL) at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory.

title: Clarifying BBL's Folding Mechanism: Non-Cooperative, Barrierless Folding from Enhanced MD and Chemical Shift Analysis
abstract: Accurate structural characterization across thermal folding/unfolding transitions is essential for understanding protein folding mechanisms. Here, we combine extensive molecular dynamics simulations with LEGOLAS, a fast and scalable machine-learning-based NMR chemical shift predictor, to map the complex folding landscape of BBL, the peripheral subunit-binding domain from Escherichia coli 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase (PDB: 2CYU). BBL has two stable helical regions (referred to as helix 1 and helix 2), linked together by a very flexible region.

title: SACred: mining the Protein Data Bank for single-atom catalyst sites
abstract: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) are built from a small set of sites, most often a metal held by four nitrogens, while enzymes run hydrogen evolution, O2 and CO2 reduction and N2 fixation on single metals in many different first coordination shells. Here we mine that diversity. SACred, an automated pipeline built and run with AI agents, reduces every transition-metal site of the Protein Data Bank (PDB) to its first coordination shell, turns the recurring shells into candidate SAC sites and screens them in a funnel: each shell is mapped onto a single or double vacancy in graphene, screened with…

title: [HYD-Py] 3 : light- and acid-driven reversible in-plane ring breathing between physicochemically and functionally distinct expanded and contracted states of an 18-membered nonaazamacrocycle
abstract: Stimuli-responsive macrocycles can alter shape through conformational reorganization or changes in covalent connectivity, but repeatable, connectivity-preserving resizing of an intact ring has remained elusive. Here we report [HYD-Py] 3 , an 18-membered nonaazamacrocycle that undergoes reversible in-plane ring breathing while preserving atom count and bonding topology. Condition-selective divergent cyclotrimerization of a bifunctional pyridine monomer furnishes expanded all-trans and contracted all-cis states, the latter locked by a cyclic array of three intramolecular N–H···N hydrogen bonds.

title: Total Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Cannalactone, a Noncanonical Strigolactone from Hemp
abstract: Strigolactones (SLs) are apocarotenoid phytohormones secreted by plants into the rhizosphere. They act as signaling molecules for the development of arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi. SLs also play a crucial role in stimulating the seed germination of root parasitic plants such as Orobanche , Phelipanche , and Striga , which are among the most threatening weeds to major crops worldwide. Phelipanche ramosa primarily infests rapeseed, hemp, and tobacco, with population P. ramosa 2a preferentially attacking hemp and population P. ramosa 1 targeting rapeseed.

title: λproc: a compositional language for process description, with a case study in chemical synthesis
abstract: Processes—cooking recipes, formulations, industrial flowsheets, chemical synthesis procedures—are recorded as prose or as diagrams. Neither form is machine-checkable, neither admits a canonical string, and neither makes the reuse of a sub-process explicit. We present λproc, a language in which a process is written as a composition of functions over streams: a unit operation is a function from streams to streams, a sub-process is a named lambda, and the process graph is not drawn but emerges from referential transparency—two textual mentions of the same expression denote the same physical…

title: Mechanistic Pitfalls of Unbalanced Excited-State Descriptions across Competing Pathways: Thiophene as a Case Study
abstract: A balanced description of excited states remains challenging even for small organic molecules. For thiophene, we show that an unbalanced description can conceal an entire relaxation pathway. Comparing SA-CASSCF and RMS-CASPT2 potential energy curves toward the ring-opening (RO) and ring-puckering (RP) conical intersections, we identify the state carrying the molecule to each crossing, termed the carrier state. Dynamic electron correlation leaves the RO carrier (πσ*) state nearly unchanged but strongly stabilizes the RP carrier (ππ*) state.

title: Materials Acceleration Platform Enables Material-Efficient High-Throughput Study of n-Doped Conjugated Polymers
abstract: This paper describes a material-efficient method to evaluate the performance of n-type conjugated polymers using the RoboMapper Material Acceleration Platform across a large parameter space. We utilize the platform to investigate the n-doping of the benchmark N2200 polymer, which we synthesized in a small batch size, utilizing n-DMBI across 112 processing conditions, spanning solvent composition, dopant concentration, and annealing temperature. Material usage is reduced by 83 % compared to conventional spin-coating.

title: Binding of legacy and emerging PFAS to Na-and Ca-montmorillonite basal surfaces: roles of the exchangeable cation and layer-charge heterogeneity, with implications for vadose-zone leaching
abstract: Clay minerals are widely assumed to retard per-and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in soils, yet the strength and mechanism of PFAS binding to smectites are unresolved: measured montmorillonite Kd values span two orders of magnitude, and the only published free-energy simulation of PFAS on smectite predicts logKd values higher than any measurement. We combined umbrella-sampling molecular dynamics of ten legacy and emerging PFAS (C4–C8 perfluoroalkyl carboxylates and sulfonates, GenX, ADONA, 6:2 FTS and F-53B) on Na-and Ca-montmorillonite with a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model of…

title: Non-compliant site welding of thermomechanically treated reinforcing bars: joint efficiency, failure mode and code conformance of three commercial grades
abstract: Butt-welded splices in reinforcing bars are routinely made on South Asian construction sites with general-purpose rutile electrodes, without preheat or procedure qualification. This study examines the consequences for three commercial thermomechanically treated (TMT) bars, B500CWR (10 mm), B500DWR (16 mm) and B600D-R (16mm),joinedbyshieldedmetalarcweldingwithE6013 electrodes under those conditions.

title: Quantifying trends across a series of leaving groups in mixtures containing ionic liquids
abstract: The nucleofugality of fluoride was measured in a range of solvent mixtures containing ionic liquids. The first order rate constants associated with the solvolysis of the fluorides of well-described electrofuges were determined in mixtures of ethanol and different proportions of the ionic liquid 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide. Temperature-dependent kinetic analyses allowed determination of activation parameters and rationalisation of observed solvent effects in different ionic liquid mixtures through consideration of solvent interactions with species along the…

title: Environmental Selection of Thymine over Uracil in Prebiotic Chemical Evolution: Insights from a Kinetic Monte Carlo Model
abstract: The replacement of uracil (U) by thymine (T) is a defining chemical feature of the transition from RNA-to DNA-based heredity. While thymine’s superior stability is well known, the role of prebiotic environmental conditions in driving this selection remains quantitatively underexplored. Here we present a stochastic kinetic Monte Carlo model (UPDSF v4.4) that simulates competition between uracil and thymine across four archetypal prebiotic environments using strictly literature-derived parameters. Molecular fitness is quantified by a Stability-Kinetics Ratio (Sr = τ_stable / κ_poly).

title: EVALUATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, PHYSICOCHEMICAL CHARACTERISTICS, PHYTOCHEMICAL CONSTITUENTS AND GC-MS ANALYSIS OF POLYALTHIA LONGIFOLIA ETHANOL LEAF EXTRACTS
abstract: In the array of traditional medicine, Polyalthia longifolia is one of the highly esteemed plants because of its high potency for curing numerous diseases. The plant contains various bioactive compounds that promote a healthy life. Purpose: This study involves the assessment of the impact of environmental conditions on the physicochemical properties, phytochemical analysis, and the GC-MS characterization of bioactive chemicals in polyalthia longifolia leaf extracts. Design of study: The leaf sample was taken at various times, including 6:00 a.m., 1:00 p.m., and 6:00 p.m.

title: De Novo Design of Blood-Brain Barrier-Penetrant, P-Glycoprotein-Evading EGFR Inhibitors and Hypoxia-Activated Trapping Analogs for Glioblastoma
abstract: Background: Most Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM) tumors about 50% grow because of a very overreactive protein called EGFR (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor). Existing drugs like Erlotinib and Gefitinib work great for lung cancer, but they are not effective for brain cancer and subsequently fail for three main reasons. First, they are too water-attracting (polar, with TPSA > 74 Å2), and second, they are very heavy with a molecular weight above 390 Da. Due to all of these factors, they are unable to cross the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB).

title: Translational Potential of New Academic Synthetic Transformations: Lessons from the Aza Paternò–Büchi Reaction
abstract: Despite steady advances in synthetic methodology, the reactions routinely used in medicinal chemistry have changed little over several decades, which suggests that discovering a reaction and establishing it as a practical tool are separate challenges. Academic methods are typically judged by yield, selectivity, and scope, whereas industrial adoption also depends on supply-chain security, reagent availability, and scalability.

title: Stackable Force Fields in GROMACS: Addons and Mixed 1–4 Scaling
abstract: Hybrid biomolecular simulations routinely combine building blocks described by different force fields, yet the GROMACS topology format and its preprocessing tools have long assumed a single, monolithic force field whose 1–4 electrostatic and Lennard-Jones scaling factors are global to the whole system. We introduce force field addons: self-contained .ffa directories that contribute atom types, bonded parameters, and residue, hydrogen, and terminus databases to a base force field at gmx pdb2gmx run time, with explicit compatibility declarations, priority-based resolution of overlapping…

title: Improving Structure Prediction for Intrinsically Disordered Proteins: High-Throughput Ensemble Generation via Torsion-Space Sampling and OpenMM Vacuum Relaxation
abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) challenge traditional structural biology paradigms due to their lack of a unique tertiary structure. Structure prediction tools, including AlphaFold, frequently fail when applied to IDPs, artificially collapsing dynamic ensembles into static, over-compacted, or incorrect structures. Here, we present an improved, streamlined pipeline tailored for generating valid, highly variable starting conformational ensembles for high-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) simulations by integrating and optimizing existing sampling techniques.

title: OlefinCat-LLM: Full-Text Extraction and Chemistry-Guarded Ranking of Single-Site Polyolefin Catalyst–Process Packages
abstract: An industrial polyolefin grade, whether an EPDM tire compound or a solution-process polyolefin elastomer, is specified by melt index or Mooney viscosity, but it is made by a precatalyst package (metal center, ligand family, and activator role) and by a polymerization window of temperature T , pressure P , and Al/M ratio. Those fields sit in the nested experimental tables of papers and patents.

title: Sulfur Nitrosylation by Cytochrome P460 Can Complete the Catabolic Primary Metabolism of Ammonia Oxidizing Bacteria
abstract: Ammonia oxidizing bacteria (AOB) generate reducing equivalents for cellular respiration via the multi-electron oxidation of ammonia (NH3) to nitrite (NO2–). Two steps are known: the hydroxylation of NH3 to hydroxylamine (NH2OH) by ammonia monooxygenase, and the oxidation of hydroxylamine NH2OH to nitric oxide (NO) via hydroxylamine oxidoreductase. However, the details of the process by which NO is oxidized by one electron to NO2– remain unknown.

title: Electrochemistry in air enabled by electric-field spillover at three-phase interfaces
abstract: Electric-field spillover at dielectric/electrolyte/electrode interfaces drives electrochemical reactions in traditionally forbidden environments, including insulating liquids and gases. Here, we show that ferrocene present in either air or toluene undergoes concerted electron- and phase-transfer at the molecularly thin 3-phase boundary, resulting in its oxidation and the transfer of the reaction product, ferrocenium, into the aqueous phase.

title: Redox Activation and Electric-Field Control of Spin Localization in a Diamagnetic Hexavanadate
abstract: Electrical control of molecular spins typically exploits pre-existing paramagnetic centers. Employing a synthetically widely used redox-active Lindqvist-type hexavanadate as a model platform, we combine density functional theory (DFT) with spin dynamics simulations of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) to establish the relationship between molecular charging, spin localization, and magnetic response.

title: Modeling IR and VCD Spectra of L-Phenylalanine Polymorphs with Polarizable Force Field Molecular Dynamics
abstract: Building on the computational framework developed by Bowles et al. [J. Chem. Phys. 158, 094305 (2023)] for IR and VCD spectroscopy of alanine in the gas and condensed phases, we employ a polarizable AMOEBA-based approach to investigate solid-state vibrational spectra. We investigate the vibrational properties of two distinct L-phenylalanine (Phe, C9H11NO2) polymorphs: the anhydrous Powder form and the hemi-hydrated Fiber structure.

title: Tailoring Amorphous Solid-state Electrolytes through Inorganic Crosslinking
abstract: Amorphous solid-state electrolytes (a-SSEs) are promising for all-solid-state batteries, but their synthesis remains empirical because network formation is poorly understood. Inspired by step-growth polymerization, we describe mechanochemical a-SSE formation as inorganic crosslinking, in which lithium-salt anions link metal-halide centers through precursor activation, oligomerization, network crosslinking, and kinetic arrest.

title: Multi-output neural network surrogate for double-pulse femtosecond optothermal control of thin silicon films on fused silica
abstract: We introduce a multi-output feedforward neural network surrogate trained on a coupled multiple-reflection and two-temperature model to map double-pulse femtosecond laser excitation (1030 nm) of crystalline silicon films on fused silica across film thicknesses (50-500 nm) and inter-pulse delays (0-10ps). Trained via Levenberg-Marquardt optimization on 2000 physical simulations, the dual-hidden-layer network ([40,30] neurons) simultaneously predicts six strongly coupled optothermal observables, peak electron temperature, peak lattice temperature, peak carrier density, minimum and maximum absorptivity and minimum refractive index achieving coefficients of determination R2 larger than 0.9998 across all targets. Evaluating a dense 200 by 200 design grid in milliseconds resolves pronounced thin-film interference fringes and carrier-induced index modulation, identifying an optimal optothermal coupling regime at d=156 nm and Dt=4.572 ps. This unified machine-learning workflow eliminates computationally expensive multi-physics runtime bottlenecks for real-time laser processing control and inverse photonic thin-film design.

title: Machine Learning the $GW$ Self-Energy Operator for Real Materials
abstract: Machine learning of $GW$ in solids has largely focused on prediction of scalar quasiparticle energy corrections. Here, we introduce a phase-aware many-body transformer that predicts the full $\mathbf{k}$-resolved complex self-energy matrix. As a proof of principle, we apply the model to predict quasiparticle energies before and after diagonalization of the quasiparticle Hamiltonian, obtaining a test set mean absolute error (MAE) of 29 meV for a dataset of 1745 2D materials in the static COHSEX approximation and 60 meV for a more limited dataset of 433 materials calculated within a plasmon-pole model. COHSEX pretraining followed by finetuning reduces this MAE to 42 meV. The predicted matrices also accurately reproduce QP wavefunctions.

title: Estimating Outpatient Visit Prices from Hospital Price Transparency Data using Large Language Models
abstract: Objective: Hospital care prices in the United States have increased substantially, yet patients lack effective tools to access and compare costs. We aimed to develop and evaluate an LLM-based approach for improving access to and use of hospital price transparency (PT) data. Materials and Methods: To estimate visit prices, we used a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework to analyze PT files from three major hospitals in Maryland and the surrounding region. We compared BM25, OpenAI embedding models, and a GPT-BM25 hybrid against a no-RAG baseline for cost estimation of individual procedures and procedure groups, then evaluated the best approach for symptom-based visit cost estimation using synthetic simulations. Results: Across hospitals, the GPT-BM25 retriever achieved the best performance, with average price MAPE of 19.44% for individual procedures and 4.90% for groups, compared with 147.98% and 82.82%, respectively, for the no-RAG baseline. In simulations, our framework correctly identified approximately 50% of reference procedures and reduced MAPE relative to the LLM-only baseline at two of the three hospitals, while achieving comparable performance at the third. Discussion: Our framework uses RAG to improve care price estimation in real-world settings. Compared with the no-RAG baseline, it substantially improved cost estimates for both individual procedures and procedure groups. Improvements were smaller in synthetic simulations, likely because inferring procedures from clinical information is more complex. Practical challenges remain, including heterogeneous PT file formats, unexplained duplicate entries, and limited availability of insurer-negotiated rates. Conclusion: LLMs that effectively integrate PT data show strong potential to provide patients with more accessible and accurate healthcare cost estimates.

title: Oxygens breathe, electrons jump
abstract: Electronic transport in polyanionic battery cathodes proceeds through small-polaron hopping between transition-metal sites and is commonly assumed to be tightly coupled to the motion of charge-compensating mobile ions. Using olivine Li$_x$MnPO$_4$ as a prototypical platform, we use first-principles molecular dynamics with extended Hubbard functionals to follow, in real time and at finite temperature, the adiabatic evolution of Mn oxidation states and atomic sublattices. We find that polaron hopping and cation migration are dynamically decoupled: Mn$^{2+}$/Mn$^{3+}$ valence exchanges occur frequently while the intercalated ions remain confined to their sites, and hopping is gated by the local oxygen framework. Freezing the six oxygen atoms of an individual MnO$_6$ octahedron excludes that site from the hopping network, while increasing the fictitious oxygen mass slows down electronic transport. Each valence exchange coincides with a concerted breathing of the donor and acceptor octahedra ($ΔV \simeq 2$ $Å^3$), with their volume asymmetry crossing zero at the transition, consistent with the Holstein-Marcus coincidence condition. The hopping rate yields an activation energy of $E_a = 0.20 \pm 0.03$ eV, closely matching the elastic energy scale of the two coordination cages ($λ_V/4 \approx 0.20$ eV). These results identify the oxygen coordination cage, not the mobile cation sublattice, as the dynamical gate for small-polaron transport: a site can accept the electron only if its cage can breathe, and the barrier is governed by cage elasticity. Selective constraints and mass scaling applied to first-principles dynamics provide a general route to link electronic and lattice degrees of freedom in redox-active materials, opening the door to framework engineering in intercalation and mixed ionic-electronic conductors.

title: Fast and background-suppressed DNA-PAINT
abstract: The speed and resolution of DNA-PAINT imaging is partly limited by the background fluorescence at high imager-strand concentrations. Here, we combine the photoactivatable fluorophore-quencher-DNA probes with the photoactivation, diffusion, and excitation strategy on a spinning disk confocal microscope, decoupling background fluorescence from the imager-strand concentration. This method yields >7-fold faster DNA-PAINT imaging in cells, a ~15 nm localization precision in hydrogels, without using specialized or speed-optimized imager strands.

title: When Do Tensor Product Paths Matter? A Group-Theoretic Analysis of Equivariant Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Tensor-product (TP) layers in equivariant interatomic potentials encode angular interactions through symmetry-allowed paths. Yet local site symmetry can make an allowed path carry no signal after neighbor aggregation. We call this effect Aggregation Cancellation. In a scalar-input first layer, equal-species neighbors on a complete site-symmetry orbit share scalar and radial factors, reducing their angular contribution to a spherical-harmonic orbit sum. If the restricted degree-$l$ representation has no trivial component, this sum and the corresponding path vanish for any learned radial weight. For an ideal $O_h$ octahedral orbit, this removes the $l_\mathrm{edge}=1,2,3$ classes. Beyond the first layer, the factorisation no longer holds, so cancellation is no longer guaranteed; we instead ask whether affected paths remain less important on average. We test the two levels separately in NequIP: matched-radius TiO$_6$ probes examine first-layer cancellation, whereas a within-model CaTiO$_3$ comparison and six OMat24 models examine the importance bias. We then rank paths on training frames, choose the pruning fraction on validation frames, and evaluate frozen masks on held-out tests. At the highest evaluated fraction (60% of 174 paths), force mean absolute error (MAE) changes are 1.42%, 0.04%, and 1.83% for CaTiO$_3$, OMat24 $O_h$-cubic, and OMat24 low-symmetry data, respectively. The masks imply 67.12-71.94% potential TP-operation reduction and 59.77% potential edge multilayer perceptron (MLP) reduction; these are structural proxies, not measured speedups. The results connect local symmetry to path redundancy and pruning robustness in NequIP; transfer to other architectures remains open.

title: Unified Deep Learning Framework for Interpretable Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries under Stochastic Group-Behavioral Usage Scenarios.
abstract: With the widespread use of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) across various industries, accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is essential for end-users. However, stochastic degradation patterns under unpredictable real-world operations pose a fundamental challenge to conventional prognostic models. This study develops a unified deep learning-based framework for RUL prediction under group-behavioral usage scenarios.

title: Tycholyzer: NanoTemper NT.6 Tycho Analysis Tool
abstract: NanoTemper Tycho NT.6 is a nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nanoDSF) instrument that enables rapid measurement of apparent protein melting temperatures. Thermal shift assays are widely used to assess protein stability under different conditions, including screening for protein-ligand interactions. These experiments often involve multiple samples, conditions, and replicates collected across several instrument runs, generating datasets that can be cumbersome to organize, compare, and analyze quantitatively. Here, we introduce Tycholyzer, a user-friendly software application that streamlines processing and analysis of Tycho nanoDSF data. Tycholyzer allows users to combine data from multiple runs, inspect and select individual fluorescence traces, and normalize and group replicate profiles for comparison across experimental conditions. The software provides two complementary approaches for determining apparent melting temperatures: sigmoidal fitting of fluorescence ratio profiles and identification of extrema in their first derivatives. Automated fitting of individual replicates enables calculation of mean melting temperatures and standard deviations, facilitating quantitative assessment of experimental variability. By integrating these capabilities into a single graphical interface, Tycholyzer promotes consistent, efficient, and rigorous analysis of nanoDSF experiments. Tycholyzer is freely available and can be run in MATLAB or as a standalone application using MATLAB Runtime (https://github.com/VGhani/Tycholyzer.git).

title: Giant Raman Optical Activity in Chiral and Polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$
abstract: Raman optical activity (ROA) measures the difference in Raman scattering intensity for right- and left-circularly polarized light and reflects the chirality of excitations. In solids, ROA is commonly very weak. For the phonons of chiral and polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$, we find a giant ROA with magnitude 100 times higher than commonly reported for molecules. The systematic analysis based on phonon selection rules allows the chiral and achiral scattering channels to be separated. First-principles calculations of the Raman tensor at finite phonon momentum relate the effect to the phonon modulation of the band-geometric and band-dispersion contributions to optical gyrotropy. This establishes Raman optical activity as a probe of electron--phonon modulation of the band geometry in an insulator.

title: On the richness of metamaterials generated by recursive cell division
abstract: Scale-rich metamaterials are one member of a family of recursive cell divisions, which differ in which cell is cut, where the cut passes and at what angle. We characterise six members of this family through three network mappings, the cell tree, the dual graph of ligaments and junctions, and the frame graph of spans, and through their elastic-wave properties: the effective refractive index n, its isotropy and the band over which it holds. The dual-graph degree law, the mean degree and the age law of the ligaments hit by new ones are the same for every rule, so they cannot distinguish the materials. The cell tree and the cell shapes do differ, and one consequence of them explains the physics: the tail of long spans in the frame graph. With the longest spans as the length scale, the bending part of the inverse squared index follows a single power law across rules, densities and numbers of ligaments, and the same spans set the lowest local resonance and the band edge. The stretching part, which caps the index, is carried by the straight frame lines of the tiling rather than by the division. Random cut angles produce elongated cells and long spans, hence high index and a narrow band; cuts perpendicular to the long axis of the cell keep the cells compact, giving low index and a wide band. Cutting through the centroid instead of a random point bounds the split fraction between 4/9 and 5/9, which removes the area hierarchy without changing the index. The cut angle interpolates continuously between these limits, and the isotropy peaks where the ligament orientations become isotropic while the cells are still compact. In three dimensions the plate and strut divisions are stretching dominated and the index stays low for every rule.

title: An Exploration of Physical and Chemical Representation in Coarse-Grained, Machine-Learned Protein Models
abstract: Machine-learned coarse-graining has emerged as a reliable framework for building protein models that accurately and efficiently sample their relevant conformational landscape. Existing studies assume a predefined map from full- to coarse-grained resolution. However, the choice of map strongly affects the quality of the models. Here, we study the dependence of system-specific machine-learned coarse-grained (MLCG) models across 7 mapping choices, spanning different resolutions and embedding types for coarse-grained beads. We show that resolution and chemical diversity do not always correlate with accuracy, and that accurate protein-specific models can be generated using minimal chemical diversity if the latent space representation of the system has high enough dimensionality.

title: Metallic or insulating magnetic phases of transition-metal oxides in light of the Slater vs Mott controversy
abstract: Magnetic d-electron oxides usually have a long-range-ordered ground state and an above-ground-state disordered para phase. The historical Slater-Mott controversy still reverberating to date pertains to understanding the origin of the insulating vs metallic nature of these two phases. Slater suggested that the insulating character evolved from the long-range order (LRO) antiferromagnetic (AFM) cell-doubling, leading to energy band repulsion and thus to forming a band gap. The reliance on LRO to explain gapping suggests that the absence of LRO in the spin-disordered para-phase would deprive the system from band repulsion, thus predicting a metallic paramagnetic (PM) phase. This, however, conflicts with numerous current observations. The alternative Mott-Peierls-Hubbard view abandons the mean-field-like band structure view emphasizing instead the local interelectronic repulsion U as a strong correlation signature of gapping both at the presence or absence of LRO. However, U is not an easily measured or calculated quantity in periodic systems, a situation often leading in practice to treating U as an adjustable parameter. The current work uses a parameter-free mean-field-like approach (Density Functional Theory, DFT), allowing energy-lowering symmetry breaking. This is done by considering local magnetic motifs as building blocks of the macroscopic AFM or PM phases. It is found that even when such motifs are isolated electronically from each other (i.e. vanishing LRO) by embedding them in quantum barriers (such as magnetic NiO6 octahedra surrounded locally by wide-gap MgO) they exhibit an intrinsic band gap. Thus, the origin of the band gaps in AFM or PM phases need not be LRO or strong correlation and can be understood within the mean-field-like band structure approach with symmetry breaking.

title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
abstract: Lab-in-the-loop systems, in which a model proposes molecules, automated assays measure their properties and the results retrain the model, are a popular approach to antibody lead optimization. These systems optimize for a specification defined with metrics computed from instrument signals, so their success depends on how well those metrics serve as proxies for the properties a drug candidate needs. When a metric is a poor proxy, neither a better model nor more data will fix it, and identifying the problem usually requires expert review. We report two campaigns run on BigHat Biosciences' Milliner platform, one on an anti-albumin nanobody (VHH) and one on an anti-mesothelin single-chain variable fragment (scFv), in which a research team and a general-purpose AI agent, Claude, brought scientific reasoning into the loop. Over seven rounds and about 1,010 design variants we built libraries from antibody lineage, structure and biophysics, and found from the raw curves that on each scaffold one thermal metric did not measure what its name implied. The libraries were built as controlled comparisons, so the results also show what each mutation contributes to each property. We fit a physical model of the curves, used it to choose metrics suited to each scaffold, and changed the experimental protocol, varying protein concentration and heating rate, to test the model against pre-registered predictions. Both leads improve on their parents in affinity, thermal stability and aggregation while improving or maintaining yield and purity.

title: Spectroscopic evidence for unconventional surface magnetism in the Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$
abstract: Kondo insulators have a non-magnetic bulk due to many-body screening of local moment by conduction electrons. However, the surface of these systems has reduced density of itinerant electrons and may experience a Kondo breakdown, leading to recovery of non-zero local moments and possible magnetic order. Here we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate the (010) surface of a $d$-$p$ electron Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$, which is predicted to host a bulk $d$-wave altermagnetic state in the absence of Kondo screening. We find anisotropic splitting on the surface states with a maximum in the $k_z$ direction and a minimum in the $k_x$ direction. The splitting is apparently suppressed with increasing temperature or with Te doping, suggesting that the splitting arises from a magnetic order rather than Rashba effects. Considering the proximity of the bulk to a $d$-wave altermagnetic state and considering the symmetry of the crystal on the surface, we postulate that our observations may be consistent with an emergent surface altermagnetic order. Such an unconventional 2-dimensional magnetic order naturally hosted on an insulating, non-magnet bulk substrate may offer a promising platform for versatile applications.
authors: Erin E. Fleck Jonathan A. Sobota

title: Thermodynamics of Metal–Hydroxide Interactions
abstract: Metal-bound hydroxide species play central roles in biological catalysis, ligand exchange, and metal-ion selectivity, but their accurate representation in classical molecular dynamics simulations remains challenging because of the strong electrostatic and ion-induced dipole interactions associated with hydroxide coordination. In this work, we develop 12–6–4 Lennard-Jones nonbonded parameters for metal–hydroxide interactions involving Mg(II), Ca(II), Mn(II), Fe(II), Co(II), Ni(II), Cu(II), Zn(II), and Cd(II) in both TIP3P and OPC water models. The hydroxide–water C4 parameter was first optimized to reproduce the experimental hydration free energy of hydroxide, followed by systematic optimization of metal–hydroxide C4 terms against experimental metal–hydroxide binding free energies derived from stability constants. Potential of mean force calculations were used for parameter refinement, while thermodynamic integration calculations provided an independent validation through closed thermodynamic cycles. The optimized parameters reproduce experimental binding affinities within chemical accuracy for both water models and correct the severe overbinding observed with conventional 12–6 and default 12–6–4 models. Structural validation against density functional theory calculations further shows that the modified parameters provide reasonable metal–oxygen distances, with the OPC water model generally giving closer agreement with quantum mechanical geometries. Analysis of the potential of mean force (PMF) profiles reveals ligand-exchange barriers and solvent-mediated second-shell intermediates during hydroxide dissociation. Overall, the resulting parameter set provides a classical framework for modeling metal–hydroxide interactions in aqueous and biological environments where both thermodynamic accuracy and structural realism are required.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
